tldr: Page 69 survey responses reveal sharp ideological divide on Oregon's prosperity: progressives strongly advocate for expanded Preschool for All (citing 3-to-1 ROI and 22% family income gains), universal childcare, and wealth-based taxation; conservatives demand business tax cuts (especially CAT elimination), deregulation, and faster permitting. Shared concerns span housing affordability, childcare costs exceeding wages, small-business sustainability, and public safety/homelessness.

bullets.text: Multiple respondents cite Preschool for All delivering '3-to-1 return on investment' and raising 'family incomes by about 22% on average,' described as a 'three-generation poverty reducer.'
Progressive respondents advocate wealth-based taxation, referencing Washington State's Millionaire tax model, closing passive income loopholes, and state-funded non-profit housing.
Conservative respondents demand CAT tax elimination, cuts to personal and corporate income taxes, gas tax reductions, and simplified tax codes.
Permitting delays and high development costs cited as major barriers; respondents request streamlined approval processes, 25-40% faster timelines, reduced development fees, and BOLI law changes.
Energy policy divide: conservatives advocate coal, natural gas, dam rebuilding, and logging expansion; progressives support hydro-electric and geothermal investment.
Childcare affordability crisis documented with childcare costs exceeding mortgage payments; widespread advocacy for universal free childcare ages 0-5 and statewide Preschool for All expansion.
Small business owners report high tax burden, slow permitting timelines, excessive development fees; request targeted tax credits, streamlined processes, and enterprise/opportunity zone incentives.
Governor Kotek specifically criticized; calls for leadership change, state audit of spending and fraud investigation, and policy prioritizing workers and families over wealthy interests.
Public safety and homelessness identified as prosperity barriers; concerns raised about street drug use, homeless encampments, insufficient law enforcement response, and immigration enforcement.
